Really though, for most people I know this is a question of short-term benefit vs. long-term benefit. Which often boils down to distraction vs. discipline. And barely anyone is good at that when confronted with the myriad of distractions that you are presented with because others profit from those distractions of yours.

What helps is motivation, but I don't know how to enforce that. The other thing that helps is creating a work environment that fights distractions (a computer where certain websites are blocked in your hosts file, a room without telephones, etc). Basically find a way to minimize distractions, whatever they may be for you, for the time you want to be focussed.

I even create such time bubbles for playing video games, because the amount of distractions out there has become such a monster, that it would prevent me from having fun if I don't shield myself. I'm talking about games that require you to invest some time, not these mobile app games that are essentially just another form of short-term distraction.
